prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: transparent PNG 2D skeletal animation parts atlas for the existing BlitzWord game.
Reference image: the attached approved Rowanfire boys lineup. Use ONLY the ARCHER BOY ON THE RIGHT as the exact identity reference. Preserve his chestnut side-swept hair, warm skin, large brown eyes, youthful proportions, forest-green woodland cloak with gold leaves/red rowan berries, rust-red hood collar, cream sleeves, green tunic, brown belt, leather bracers, leggings and boots, wooden bow and quiver. Do not include mage or knight.
Primary request: Prepare a professional, cleanly separated painted puppet parts atlas for this same boy, for a battle facing screen RIGHT in a slight three-quarter view. The face must still be recognizably this exact boy, looking right with a focused gentle expression. Preserve the rich polished storybook illustration style and crisp warm dark outlines. These are reusable production body parts, not a diagram or finished assembled character.
Canvas: 1536 by 1536, genuinely transparent alpha background. Exactly 4 equal columns and 4 equal rows of invisible 384x384 cells. Exactly one isolated part centered in each cell with generous transparent margins; no part crosses a cell. No grid, no labels, no numbers, no shadows on the background. Each part fills its own cell as much as possible, so we will scale the parts when assembling. Do not keep the parchment background.
Read cells left-to-right, top-to-bottom:
Row 1: (1) head plus short neck, exact approved chestnut boy identity, slight three-quarter facing right; (2) entire torso from neck to tunic hem with red hood collar, leafy green shoulder mantle, gold flower clasp, diagonal leather strap, belt and pouches, NO head, NO arms, NO hands, NO legs, completely painted where arms used to cover torso; (3) long green back cloak only, separate draped fabric with rowan/gold leaf motifs, no torso or limbs; (4) quiver with a few arrows, no body.
Row 2: (5) bow-side upper arm, cream sleeve from rounded shoulder to rounded elbow, straight pointing DOWN; (6) bow-side forearm with brown leather bracer, elbow to wrist, straight pointing DOWN, NO hand; (7) string-side upper arm, cream sleeve rounded shoulder to elbow, straight pointing DOWN; (8) string-side forearm with brown leather bracer, elbow to wrist, straight pointing DOWN, NO hand.
Row 3: (9) small left hand curled naturally around an empty vertical bow grip, fingers visible, NO bow; (10) small right drawing hand in three-finger archery string grip, NO arrow and NO string; (11) relaxed right release hand with slightly opened fingers; (12) the approved curved wooden bow by itself, vertical, curved bulge to the RIGHT and tips on the LEFT, leather central grip, NO hand, NO string, NO arrow, full bow visible.
Row 4: (13) far upper leg from hip to knee in dark olive/brown leggings, down-pointing; (14) far lower leg and complete brown leather boot pointing screen RIGHT, rounded knee at top; (15) near upper leg from hip to knee in matching leggings, down-pointing; (16) near lower leg and complete brown leather boot pointing screen RIGHT, rounded knee at top.
Part construction: joint ends should have rounded overlapping painted caps so they rotate without gaps. Clothing and skin continue under overlaps. Keep limbs short and childlike matching the reference. Separate pieces must never include duplicate attached body parts. The shoulder mantle belongs to torso; each upper arm is just cream sleeve. Keep original rich painted detail and character identity, not flat vector, not generic fantasy, not photoreal or 3D. Export with actual transparent pixels, not a drawn checkerboard.
status: Prototype artwork; final character approval pending. Existing production assets are preserved.
